title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stock in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll be linking a detailed spreadsheet that tracks the breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Overall: Positive

The major indices continued to grind higher last week, with large caps leading the advance while mid- and small-cap indices showed healthy, if somewhat lagging, price action. Notably, mid- and small-cap benchmarks are working to break out to new short-term highs just a few days after the large caps achieved theirs, reflecting constructive follow-through.

Supporting this price action, all four major indices remain above their rising 10-, 20-, and 50-day moving averages, highlighting the strength of both short-term and intermediate-term trends. Minor pullbacks and consolidations are to be expected, but as long as the indices hold these intermediate-term moving averages and avoid heavy distribution, the market environment should continue to favor the long side.

Beneath the surface, market internals remain encouraging. Breadth and momentum have expanded further, with stocks making new short-term highs outpacing new short-term lows by more than 2-to-1, suggesting solid participation and underlying demand. As long as breadth and momentum numbers are expanding, the stocks should have a wind at their backs. As some point these numbers will contract and reflect waning demand, but until that time we trade inline with the predominate pressures.

Sector leadership also remains supportive. Technology continues to dominate at the top of the relative strength rankings, while Industrials, Financials, and Materials are holding firm within the leadership group. These sectors reflect healthy participation across multiple styles and market themes. Notably, Consumer Discretionary—which had been a laggard in previous weeks—has shown renewed strength and is attempting to reestablish leadership.

On the weaker side, Energy, Defensive sectors, and Real Estate continue to underperform, showing persistent relative weakness and lack of strong accumulation.

Market Recap

Market Monitor (Click Here)

1. Build Exposure with Intentional Precision

Add Exposure Selectively: Add exposure to high-quality setups with strong technical patterns, prioritizing names breaking out with volume or bouncing off rising 10- or 20-day moving averages.

Avoid Chasing Strength: Even in a constructive environment, maintain discipline. Avoid extended names far above logical support. Focus instead on fresh breakouts or orderly pullbacks to support within strong relative strength themes.

Set Logical Risk Controls and Manage Positions Proactively:

  • For both new and existing positions, place stops just below recent swing lows or rising 20-day MAs to manage risk proactively.

  • Consider selling a portion of a position (e.g., 25–50%) into strength about 3–5 days after entry, or once the price reaches 2–3 times your initial risk, to lock in gains.

  • Then, trail the remaining shares on a close below the 10- or 20-day moving average to ride a potential trend while protecting profits.

2. Allocate Toward Leading and Emerging Sector Themes

Prioritize Sector Leadership: Allocate capital to sectors demonstrating sustained leadership and healthy participation:

  • Technology (leading convincingly)

  • Industrials

  • Financials

  • Materials

  • Healthcare

Watch for Consumer Discretionary Rotation: This group has shown renewed strength after lagging — consider re-engagement if relative strength improves further.

Avoid Underperformers: Continue to sidestep Energy, Real Estate, and Defensive groups, which show persistent weakness and lack of accumulation.

Focus on Strong Setups: Favor tight consolidations or clean support bounces with volume confirmation within these favored sectors.

3. Monitor Internal Indicators for Continuity or Warning Signs

Stay alert to the following:

  • Sustained Breadth: Participation remains positive with more stocks making new short-term highs than lows. As long as this holds or expands, it supports continued exposure.

  • Momentum Expansion: Upside momentum remains strong with a greater than 2-to-1 upside skew; continue to monitor for confirmation.

  • Broadening Leadership: Multiple sectors participating reinforces a healthier advance — watch for this to persist.

  • Potential Red Flags: Be prepared to scale back if high-volume down days (distribution) increase or breakouts begin to fail across leadership names.

4. Capital Deployment and Flexibility

Scale In Methodically: Increase risk exposure progressively, layering into high-conviction positions rather than all at once.

Maintain Cash Readiness: Keep 15–25% in cash to stay agile for new opportunities or if conditions shift.

Favor Liquidity and Sound Fundamentals: Stick to liquid, fundamentally supported stocks with consistent price/volume behavior. Avoid thin, speculative plays or news-driven spikes.

5. Watchlist Strategy and Tactical Rotation

Build a High-Conviction Watchlist: Identify strong leaders in Technology, Industrials, Financials, and Consumer Discretionary as they confirm leadership patterns.

Track Balanced Defensive Plays: Utilities and Healthcare can still serve as portfolio stabilizers, especially if volatility returns.

Stay Ready to Rotate: Be prepared to shift capital quickly if new leadership emerges or if existing leaders start to falter. Use relative strength, price structure, and volume as primary decision signals.

Bottom Line

The market environment has evolved from consolidation to confirmation. Strong price action, rising moving averages, and broadening sector participation support a constructive long-side approach. However, remain disciplined — monitor internals daily, focus on quality setups, and scale exposure carefully. Preparation, patience, and precision are still your best edge.
